bloques.titulo: The modal verb sollen and its attenuated form
texto: With **sollen** (duty) we indicate an instruction or task: **Du sollst im Bett bleiben** (you must stay in bed).
To formulate a more prudent and kind advice, the German uses the subjunctive **sollte**: **Du solltest dich ausruhen** (you should rest); **Sie sollten weniger arbeiten** (you should work less).
In both cases, the main verb moves at the end of the sentence in **infinitivo**.

frases.de: Herr Weber, ich fühle mich noch schwach. Was soll ich tun?
frases.es: Señor Weber, todavía me siento débil. ¿Qué debo hacer?
frases.en: Mr. Weber, I still feel weak. What should I do?

frases.de: Du sollst heute noch im Bett bleiben und viel schlafen.
frases.es: Debes quedarte hoy todavía en la cama y dormir mucho.
frases.en: You must still stay in bed today and sleep a lot.

frases.de: Und darf ich schon spazieren gehen?
frases.en: And can I go for a walk now?

frases.de: Nein, du solltest dich erst richtig ausruhen.
frases.en: No, you should get some rest first.

frases.de: Soll ich die Tabletten weiter nehmen?
frases.en: Should I keep taking the pills?

frases.de: Ja, du sollst die Tabletten morgens und abends nehmen.
frases.es: Sí, debes tomar las pastillas por la mañana y por la noche.
frases.en: Yeah, you have to take the pills in the morning and at night.
analisis: in the morning and at night

frases.de: Der Kranke soll viel warmen Tee trinken.
frases.es: El enfermo debe beber mucho té caliente.
frases.en: The sick person must drink a lot of hot tea.

frases.de: Sie sollten täglich eine halbe Stunde an der frischen Luft gehen.
frases.es: Usted debería caminar diariamente media hora al aire libre.
frases.en: You should walk in the open for half an hour.

frases.de: Wir sollen den Termin rechtzeitig absagen.
frases.es: Debemos cancelar la cita a tiempo.
frases.en: We have to cancel the appointment on time.

bloques.pregunta: What position does the main verb occupy in infinitive in a prayer with the modal «sollen»?

opciones.texto: At the end of the prayer.
opciones.explicacion: The conjugated modal verb is placed in second position and the main verb in infinitive closes the phrase.
The verb in infinitive does not precede the conjugated modal in the main prayer.
The first position corresponds to the subject or to an orational complement.

opciones.texto: A softer and courteous advice («You should.» instead of «You must.»).
opciones.explicacion: The Konjunktiv II attenuates the instruction by making it a prudent recommendation.
The categorical imposition is expressed with the indicative or with «müssen».

opciones.texto: An action concluded in the past.
opciones.explicacion: It's not a perfect form of past or preterito.
The modal verb «sollst» requires the infinitive «bleiben» at the end of the prayer.
It is conjugated form; with modal the infinitive is required.
It's a past participle, wrong here.

bloques.frase: Der Kranke ___ viel warmen Tee trinken.

opciones.explicacion: The third person singular in the verb sollen is irregular: «er soll» (no end -t).
«Sollt» corresponds to the second person of the plural («ihr»).
«Sollten» corresponds to wir, sie or Sie.

bloques.pregunta: What advice does this prayer express?
bloques.frase: Sie sollten täglich an der frischen Luft gehen.

opciones.texto: You should walk in the open every day.
opciones.explicacion: «Sie sollten» expresses a formal advice for walking outdoors («an der frischen Luft»).

opciones.texto: You must remain locked in your room.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase says exactly the opposite.

opciones.texto: You are forbidden to exercise outside.
opciones.explicacion: It does not express any prohibition.
The modal verb «soll ich» requires the infinitive «absagen» at the end.
It's a conjugated form, not allowed in this position with modal.
It's the perfect participle, not the infinitive.

bloques.frase: Du sollst heute im Bett bleiben
bloques.traduccion: You must stay in bed today.
bloques.explicacion: Subject + modal sollen + supplements + infinitive at the end.

intro: When we want to advise someone about their health or to transmit a medical recommendation, we use the modal verb **sollen**. The person giving the advice conjugates «sollen» in second position and the recommended action is moved at the end of the sentence in infinitive.
